audit.title: Chainlink Functions Tutorials

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Opens with a title and a topic list but no self-contained answer to "what are Chainlink Functions / where do I start." A lifted chunk from this page conveys only a menu. Add a lead sentence.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Strong for its size — 1 H1, clean `## Topics` list, 0 level skips, 12 well-formed bullets. Works as a chunk. No action beyond adding descriptions.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Measured 0 numerals, 0 units, no versions. Expected for a hub, but a line on supported networks or request limits would add liftable specificity.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: 14 links, 13 internal, 1 external (Playground), 0 primary sources. Internal linking is the hub's job and is fine; no authoritative concept anchor to the Functions overview/spec.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Weakest dimension — no definition of Chainlink Functions anywhere. An engine skimming this page cannot lift "Chainlink Functions is…". High-value gap.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: 0 JSON-LD, canonical MISSING, no datePublished/dateModified, no og/twitter tags. Note: head metadata could not be verified from served content — CLI should pass raw `<head>`.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: No code, which is appropriate for an index page — scored neutral, not penalized. The child tutorials carry the code.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Task-phrased labels cover "how do I call an API / post data / use secrets / automate." Missing: a "what is Chainlink Functions" framing and any troubleshooting/FAQ entry point.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Clean and consistent; "Chainlink Functions," "DON-hosted Secrets" used precisely. Strong; no action needed.

audit.summary: This is a thin navigation hub — 122 words, 12 links — routing to individual Chainlink Functions tutorials. As a hub it does one thing well: the link labels are phrased as developer tasks ("Call an API," "POST Data to an API," "Using DON-hosted Secrets"), which matches how devs and agents query. Its biggest GEO weakness is that it says nothing quotable: there is no one-sentence definition of Chainlink Functions, no specifics, and no metadata (0 JSON-LD blocks, missing canonical, no dates). For a hub page the honest verdict is "functional router, weak standalone citation target" — small surgical additions (a lead definition + per-link descriptions + schema) would lift it materially without turning it into a content page.

recommendations.title: Add a lead definition + orientation sentence
recommendations.where: immediately under the H1, before `## Topics`.
recommendations.issue: page opens straight into a callout and link list; no liftable definition.
recommendations.change: Add 2 sentences, e.g. "Chainlink Functions is a serverless developer platform that lets smart contracts fetch data from any API and run custom compute off-chain via a Decentralized Oracle Network (DON). These tutorials cover requests, secrets management, ABI encoding, and automation, from a simple computation to production automation."
recommendations.why: gives engines a verbatim-liftable definition and makes the hub answer "what is / where do I start" queries instead of only routing.

recommendations.title: Add a one-line description after each tutorial link
recommendations.issue: links are labels only, e.g. "[Use ABI encoding and decoding]" with no context.
recommendations.change: append a short gloss per item, e.g. "Call an API — make a GET request with query parameters and return the result on-chain." Convert to a two-column table (Tutorial | What it does) for cleaner extraction.
recommendations.why: descriptions capture symptom/task phrasing and let an engine justify *why* to pick a given tutorial, raising the odds this hub is cited for "how do I X with Chainlink Functions."

recommendations.title: Add page metadata / structured data
recommendations.issue: canonical MISSING, no dateModified, 0 JSON-LD blocks.
recommendations.change: emit `TechArticle` (or `CollectionPage`) JSON-LD with `name`, `about: "Chainlink Functions"`, canonical URL, and `dateModified`; add a visible "Last updated" line.
recommendations.why: freshness and canonical signals raise trust/E-E-A-T and help agents resolve the entity; note this is partly a site-level template fix.

recommendations.title: Link the canonical concept/overview page authoritatively
recommendations.issue: 0 links to a primary concept definition; only task pages and the Playground.
recommendations.change: link "Chainlink Functions" to the Functions overview/architecture page, and reference the DON concept page on first use.
recommendations.why: anchors the hub to the canonical definition, strengthening entity resolution and the canonical-hub pattern.

recommendations.title: Add a "Getting started / prerequisites" pointer
recommendations.issue: list jumps straight to tasks; no setup or troubleshooting entry point.
recommendations.change: add a short "Before you begin" link to the Functions getting-started/subscription setup, and a link to any troubleshooting/errors page.
recommendations.why: covers setup→use→debug lifecycle queries the current list omits.

antiPatterns: Undated content — no visible last-updated or dateModified signal.
Missing canonical URL and JSON-LD (metadata gap, not stuffing).
No keyword stuffing, marketing fluff, or unresolved cross-references — clean.
offPageNotes: Canonical URL, JSON-LD, and freshness cadence are likely governed by the site template/CMS, not this single page — fix at the layout level.
`llms.txt` is already referenced at the top — good site-level signal; ensure this hub and its children are enumerated there.
Head metadata could not be verified from the served content; have the CLI pass raw `<head>` for a definitive metadata read.
